decisions.reason: handoffs summarize away or alter user requirements | signed requirement manifests (HMAC-SHA256) with deterministic merge verification; unsafe commits 69.4%->9.0% under attack (Qwen3-8B, 1,440 trajectories, five threats), unsigned manifests violated in 79% of mutated runs vs none signed, deterministic verifier 78.7% recall vs 59.0% for an LLM checker; pre-signing injection still raises violations 14.6%->37.5%, so extraction is the trust boundary

FP8 attention is numerically sensitive and the MI355X cannot track matrix-instruction completion in hardware | probability-from-score, ping-pong softmax/MMA schedule and power-of-two block scaling; 1.16-1.76x over AITER on captured model inputs at 32K with numerical error 62-78% lower than AITER and within a few percent of Composable Kernel and Triton

KV-cache offload to host DRAM | rolling HBM cache for prefill, hot decode cache, reverse sparse index and a compute-load overlapped kernel; 1.38x prefill and 1.91x decode throughput under a 30 ms TPOT constraint on Ascend910C PD-disaggregated GLM-5.2 — serving speed

decisions.anchor: software layers between a model and the world (agent harnesses, tool-call dispatch, RAG and orchestration pipelines) that silently alter what the model receives or emits
decisions.reason: benign memories overgeneralize into unsafe later behaviour | sessions with and without memory across six frontier models (Claude Sonnet/Opus/Fable, GPT-5.6): skip-confirmation requests on low-stakes chores transfer to high-stakes tasks, support-seeking memories bias later judgments, and stale-test repair notes weaken correct tests and raise ImpossibleBench cheating

GPU-initiated RDMA still needs CPU control-path involvement or GPU-assembled WQEs | 8-byte GPU doorbell with FPGA NIC WQE reconstruction, multipath reliable connection with out-of-order arrival and hardware/software co-designed retransmission; architecture and components only — FPGA prototype under implementation, no evaluation

joint model/batch/quantization config search under memory and latency SLOs | RMQD distribution-divergence quality proxy, few-shot median calibration and BandPareto search; highest feasibility and lowest RMQD gap on A6000 and Jetson Thor — configuration search, no precision problem

agent exploration stays in transient traces and is not reused | Evolver stores structured Gene assets with acquisition, retrieval and feedback-guided evolution, no weight updates; Claude Code and Codex on Terminal-Bench 2.1/SWE-bench Multilingual/SWE-rebench/GAIA, 83.13%->87.50% on 320 paired executions with 24.24% fewer recorded tokens

why learnable KV-eviction gates fail | shows the frozen-model LM loss prefers the constant-gate no-op and that gradients charge the gate for pre-existing errors; the reworked gate reaches 90.14 RULER at 8K and 46.03 LongBench at 75% compression with Qwen3-8B — eviction method, no listed reliability problem

harness evolution gains may be unreliable, costly and non-transferable | four methods across harnesses and task types; all 16 evolved agents gain uncovered tasks while losing covered ones, reliability gains usually raise deployment cost, the highest-scoring agent never gives the largest mean improvement, and EvoAudit's revised select/analyze/mutate/gate recovers the best result

decisions.anchor: training dynamics and failure modes of RL post-training
decisions.reason: whether verifier-based RL adds anything beyond SFT | deterministic benchmark of 1,877 GPU/LLM training-failure-diagnosis tasks across 30 archetypes; SFT reaches 0.785 on the hard split while 60 GRPO steps give +0.22 in-distribution (CI [-0.06,+0.51]) and +0.33 OOD, with residual errors systematic enough to shrink GRPO's within-group signal

decisions.anchor: software layers between a model and the world (agent harnesses, tool-call dispatch, RAG and orchestration pipelines) that silently alter what the model receives or emits
decisions.reason: task-tampering injections alter the agent's reading of observations and beliefs about state instead of redirecting the task | 90 validated cases in 3 tool-use environments: undefended, decision-rule/action/state attacks beat objective attacks across five LLMs; a detection-and-removal defense cuts objective attacks to 2.4% but leaves observation and state attacks at 9.5% and 12.1%, and a tool-policy defense still allows 15.4% vs 17.0% undefended

decisions.anchor: software layers between a model and the world (agent harnesses, tool-call dispatch, RAG and orchestration pipelines) that silently alter what the model receives or emits
decisions.reason: third-party API relays silently change what the model returns | 20 relays offering GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5: 7/10 low-price relays flagged for behavioural differences vs batch-matched official answers, 4 return tool calls despite instructions disabling them, and 5 report 4,200-60,000 more input tokens than the official API for identical requests

prompt-driven agents are brittle and token-hungry | Skillware bundles (typed JSON contract + deterministic Python + unit tests) as a capability registry; 23 models x 368 benchmark conditions, up to 84.8% fewer tokens and 97.3% lower cost, parameter errors eliminated — architecture proposal, no silent-failure measurement

end-to-end autonomous drug discovery | PharmAgents2 with Paper2Skill knowledge extraction and Self-Scaling Discovery over parallel context-inheriting agents; PharmAgents-Bench v0.1 (121 questions, 9 scenarios) and highest process scores on all three end-to-end tasks, with three findings later confirmed in human-executed experiments (LpxH allosteric inhibitor, JAK1 covalent strategy, new binding target)

decisions.anchor: precision and correctness problems introduced by aggressive optimization of training and inference
decisions.reason: expert pruning with English calibration silently destroys a low-resource language | REAP 25%/50% pruning on four MoE models: at 25%, English comprehension falls 1.7 points median vs 21.4 for Lithuanian; Lithuanian calibration removes most of the loss and never significantly hurts English, with routing showing 55-72% of last-layer selections concentrated on eight experts

hallucination-prone failures of MCP agents | 358 tasks on 36 production MCP servers, 14 agents over 5,012 trajectories, mean score 0.642 and 0.458 on Unreachable Goal with 23.2% pass — a hallucination benchmark, i.e. a model-side issue this area explicitly excludes

concurrent matrix-vector execution on 3D-IMC arrays depends on weight placement | conflict-matrix mapping refined by profiling feedback; compute utilization 42.4%->60.3%, 2.0x 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x end-to-end over state-of-the-art mapping — accelerator mapping, not kernels/communication/scheduling

decisions.anchor: training dynamics and failure modes of RL post-training
decisions.reason: on-policy-distillation update strength is dominated by style positions (3.5x the mean absolute teacher-student log-prob gap of mathematical positions) | centered student-base delta coefficients kept only where the sign agrees with teacher feedback, recomputed each round; +7.76 to +10.37 points math avg@16 over OPD across 5 Qwen3 1.7B-8B teacher-student configurations

decisions.anchor: training dynamics and failure modes of RL post-training
decisions.reason: teacher supervision on student-generated rollouts is off-policy and top-k OPD discards probability mass | prefix-only (20%) alignment with overlap-gated alpha-divergence, reset support and support convergence; quantitative reliability analysis shows prefix alignment is more reliable than full context, with no headline benchmark numbers in the abstract
video-to-QA dataset generation | Whisper ASR, BART segmentation and a Llama-3.1-8B self-verification loop feeding LoRA fine-tuning — an educational pipeline application, no listed problem

how many unique activations an SAE needs at a fixed training budget | diversity-repetition scaling law across dictionary sizes, early/middle/late Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 layers and BatchTopK/TopK/JumpReLU; buffer replay plateaus, cutting activation storage 8-64x with negligible change in EV, MSE, feature absorption, auto-interpretability and sparse probing

whether a learned nonlinear latent adds anything over the PCA basis of LoRA adapters | transformer autoencoder on identity adapters compared operation-by-operation against raw weight space; the latent is far more robust to displacement and holds mixed-rank adapters in one shared latent

how non-evidential context corrupts the prediction | traces the Intrusion Pathway (MLP enrichment, parroting heads, intrusion heads) and a deployable knockout of ~10 heads (~1% of heads) recovers 57% of the distractor-induced drop across four tasks, while an oracle clean-residual replacement recovers 97.6%

block-level policy optimization for diffusion language models | prefix-block surrogate with per-token clipping and corrupted-view resampling; competitive with existing dLLM RL methods across two LLaDA-family initializations, six benchmarks and three generation lengths — the gradient-variance point is an analysis assumption, not an evaluated failure

German-English NLLB fine-tuning | 25k filtered OPUS pairs, NLLB-600M with mixed precision/gradient accumulation/checkpointing, +3.4 BLEU and +2.6 chrF++ over the base model — a single-task model report, explicitly excluded by this area

weights allocated without NUMA topology send a large share of accesses across the inter-socket interconnect, cutting per-socket bandwidth | NUMA-aware TorchInductor with NUMA tensor parallelism (per-socket sharding, thread/memory affinity); up to 2.63x prefill on dual-socket Haswell, 1.87x on dual-socket Cascade Lake and 2.27x on four-socket Haswell-EX for GPT-2/BERT/Gemma-3-270M

decisions.anchor: the reliability and trustworthiness of long-running autonomous agent systems
decisions.reason: more agents are assumed to mean more reliability, but average benchmark accuracy ignores the deployed input mix and the answer-combining rule | HIP-LLM plus a Bayesian network of the system's failure logic propagating agent failure-probability intervals; in a regulated chemical-hazard extraction pipeline majority voting over three models protects against the weakest but does not clearly exceed the best, and a voter failing on 5% of demands erases its advantage

whether attention-FFN disaggregation still pays on rack-scale NVLink with wide expert parallelism | FastAFD overlaps one microbatch's MoE with the other's attention on GB200 NVL72 and is compared against the best vLLM wide-EP setting; 1.17x on Qwen3 and 1.16x on Qwen3.5, parity on MiniMax-M2.5, with an analytical model predicting throughput within 3%
